plainTranslation: Person A (Mars)'s assertion and pace can meet resistance from Person B (Saturn)'s caution, conditions or limits. Person A (Mars) may experience that response as an attempt to inhibit initiative; Person B (Saturn) may interpret a stronger push as evidence that insufficient care is being taken. The square can therefore reinforce both reactions: stronger assertion meets firmer restraint. Repeated frustration can affect goodwill and leave effort directed toward resisting the other person rather than a shared intention. The same contact can also involve learning from the other's different capacity, but no repair or outcome follows automatically. It does not establish violence, a diagnosis, an obligation to stay or which person's judgment is correct.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep: Their limits and your drive grind against each other. You feel blocked, and they feel rushed. Agree on the pace out loud.
tension: At its worst, it's just a power struggle. They block. You push. They dig in. You get angry. Eventually, the relationship stops being about the original issue and becomes a fight over control. This is where the aspect can become exhausting. What could have been used to build something meaningful ends up consumed by the struggle itself.
advice: The useful distinction is discernment. Some limits are real. Some come from caution, uncertainty, or a desire to protect what matters. Some feedback helps you act with more strength. Some feedback reflects a different relationship to risk and timing. Learn the difference. Turn the no into a conversation when you can. Ask what the concern is protecting and what the action is trying to accomplish. Workable if both respect the tension; name the brake instead of fighting it in silence.
summaryShort: Their limits and your drive grind against each other.
